{{short description|None}}
[[File:Second trophée de la Coupe de la Ligue.JPG|thumb|The Coupe de la Ligue trophy]]
The [[Coupe de la Ligue]] was a [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout]] cup competition in [[Football in France|French football]] organised by the [[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] and comprises clubs of France's top football division, [[Ligue 1]], France's second division, [[Ligue 2]], and the third division, the [[Championnat National]]. The current competition was established relatively late in 1994 but another competition named Coupe de la Ligue existed from 1963 to 1965 and in 1982, a Coupe d'Été (later also called Coupe de la Ligue) was held before the start of the French league season. It was abolished after the 2019–20 season to reduce fixture congestion.<ref name=lfp>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49747220|title=French League Cup to end from 2020 'to reduce season schedule'|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 September 2019|access-date=18 September 2019}}</ref>

The most successful club in the history of the modern Coupe de la Ligue was [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], who won the cup nine times.<ref name="winners">{{cite web|url=http://www.frenchleague.com/coupeLigue/palmares.asp |title=Roll of Honour |publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel |access-date=20 February 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090216200341/http://frenchleague.com/coupeLigue/palmares.asp |archive-date=16 February 2009 }}</ref> Paris Saint-Germain also made the most appearances in the final, with ten. The venue for the final was the [[Parc des Princes]] for its first three years, until it was moved to the [[Stade de France]]. In September 2016, the LFP voted for the next three finals to be at [[Parc Olympique Lyonnais]] in Lyon, the [[Nouveau Stade de Bordeaux]] in Bordeaux, and the [[Stade Pierre-Mauroy]] in Lille, respectively.<ref>{{cite news|title=Coupe de la Ligue - Finale à Lyon en 2017, Bordeaux en 2018 et Lille en 2019|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/lille-59000/coupe-de-la-ligue-finale-a-lyon-en-2017-bordeaux-en-2018-et-lille-en-2019-01-09-2016-6086607.php|access-date=15 September 2017|work=Le Parisien|date=1 September 2016|language=fr|archive-date=9 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171009144135/http://www.leparisien.fr/lille-59000/coupe-de-la-ligue-finale-a-lyon-en-2017-bordeaux-en-2018-et-lille-en-2019-01-09-2016-6086607.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> In [[Coupe de la Ligue Final 2000|2000]], [[FC Gueugnon|Gueugnon]] became the first team outside the [[Ligue 1|top French league]] to win the tournament.<ref name="history">{{cite web|url=http://www.frenchleague.com/coupeLigue/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=7782 |title=League Cup History |date=26 March 2007 |publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel |access-date=20 February 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080219055505/http://www.frenchleague.com/coupeLigue/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=7782 |archive-date=February 19, 2008 }}</ref>

==Notes==
{{reflist|group=note}}

{{refbegin}}
:A.&nbsp;{{note|1991 offinal}}: Reims won the 1991 final 4–3 in a penalty shoot-out.
:B.&nbsp;{{note|1996 offinal}}: Metz won the 1996 final 5–4 in a penalty shoot-out.
:C.&nbsp;{{note|1997 offinal}}: Strasbourg won the 1997 final 6–5 in a penalty shoot-out.
:D.&nbsp;{{note|1998 offinal}}: Paris Saint-Germain won the 1998 final 4–2 in a penalty shoot-out.
:E.&nbsp;{{note|2004 offinal}}: Sochaux won the 2004 final 5–4 in a penalty shoot-out.
:F.&nbsp;{{note|2019 offinal}}: Strasbourg won the 2019 final 4–1 in a penalty shoot-out.
:G.&nbsp;{{note|2020 offinal}}: Paris Saint-Germain won the 2020 final 6–5 in a penalty shoot-out.
{{refend}}
